anomaly_def.Name: Transaction Lock Contention Anomaly + Storage Space Capacity Anomaly + CPU Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Composite definition: This anomaly denotes a situation in which Transaction Lock Contention, Storage Space Capacity exhaustion, and CPU Resource saturation all strike the database simultaneously, so the lock-manager, storage allocator, and CPU scheduler are each a primary, co-existing bottleneck.

Combined observable phenomena: Lengthening blocker–waiter chains, frequent deadlock victim errors, and surging lock-wait time appear in parallel with "no space left" or "cannot extend" messages for data, log, or temp areas. Checkpoints, log flushes, and space-reclamation tasks stall, causing commit freezes and widespread statement latency spikes. Host CPU utilization sits near 100 %, run-queue depths rise, and both user sessions and internal housekeeping processes (deadlock detectors, log writers, auto-extenders, cleaners) consume large amounts of CPU. Application layers experience cascading timeouts and aggressive retry storms, inflating connection pools and further amplifying contention. Monitoring views show interleaved lock, I/O-allocation, and CPU scheduler waits that are difficult to disentangle.

Causal interaction: Heavy lock contention prolongs transaction lifetimes, inflating undo/redo volume and retaining row versions that impede space reuse, thus accelerating consumption of data, log, and temp space. As free space dwindles, allocation failures force the engine to pause writers and invoke purge or auto-extension paths that hold additional locks, deepening blocking chains. Each stalled or repeatedly aborted transaction, along with intensified background housekeeping, drives CPU demand upward; the ensuing CPU saturation slows lock acquisition, deadlock detection, and space-management threads, further extending lock hold times and delaying space reclamation. The three resource crises therefore reinforce one another in a positive feedback loop that rapidly degrades throughput and can culminate in complete service unavailability unless all contributing factors are relieved together.

entry.official_description: Incorrect user-level lock name '%-.192s'. The name is empty, NULL, or can not be expressed in the current character-set.
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with concurrent transactions contending for the same logical resources, incompatible lock acquisition order, or transaction-state conflicts surfaced by the engine.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect blocking chains, reduce conflicting write overlap, shorten transaction lifetime, review lock acquisition order, and verify whether transaction scheduling or retry logic needs adjustment.
